newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippine personal care market to grow strongly.
newsitem.headline: Philippine personal care market to grow strongly.

text.p: The personal care market in the Philippines is expected to grow strongly over the next few years as increasing affluence fuels higher spending for products like body soap and shampoos, an official said on Monday.

Evelina Patino, Vice-President at United Coconut Chemicals, said at an Asia surfactants conference here the value of the personal care sector will expand by an estimated 16 percent to US$212 million market by 1998 from $183 million in 1995.
"I would expect that with increasing affluence in the Philippines, surfactant consumption will grow," she said.
The market is dominated by Procter & Gamble Co, Unilever, and Colgate-Palmolive Co.
Procter's Philippine unit has a 36 percent share of the shampoo market followed by Unilever at 28 percent and Colgate at 27 percent, she said.

Procter is also the leading company in the Philippine detergent market, which is worth about $420 million. The U.S. firm has a 41 percent share while Unilever controls 26.15 percent and Colgate has a 15.78 percent stake, she said.
Patino said the Philippines detergent industry is expected to expand by five percent a year.

"The growth of washing machine powder will also be influenced by the increasing difficulty in getting household help. Sales for washing machines doubled yearly from the year 1994 and are seen to grow until all middle-class homes will have purchased one," she said.
In the toothpaste market, Colgate has a 62 percent share of the market but this is sharply down from its 85 percent share of a decade ago. Unilever has an 18 percent share of the market.
